description: indexes.md opens by declaring two classes of indexes (Traditional and Vector) and then presents a table organised by index type and providing service. It never says how the two schemes relate - and they do not nest: a Search index is Traditional while a Search Vector index is Vector, so class cuts across service; and a Composite Vector Index is stated to BE a GSI, so class cuts across type as well. A reader trying to build a mental taxonomy from this page will build a hierarchy that the page's own examples contradict. This was round 11's headline modelling problem and the reason index-class:traditional and index-class:vector were promoted as a separate axis rather than as supertypes.
